question: Should OpenClaw adopt Claws as the experimental core contract for installing and lifecycle-managing a complete portable agent, rather than keeping this composition outside the core roadmap?
rationale: The documents define new product, compatibility, and ownership boundaries across agents, workspaces, packages, MCP configuration, and scheduled work; correctness of the prose cannot determine whether that contract is the desired product direction.

options.title: Sponsor the experimental Claws contract
options.body: Accept the RFC as the roadmap for gated implementation, retaining the stated experimental status until the package and manifest surfaces have production validation.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Keep the proposal open while maintainers decide whether portable complete-agent composition belongs in core or should remain an external extension pattern.

options.title: Narrow the RFC first
options.body: Request a reduced contract that settles agent and package ownership before specifying the remaining lifecycle surfaces.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the experimental Claws contract
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC as the roadmap for gated implementation, retaining the stated experimental status until the package and manifest surfaces have production validation.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recorded review questions directly concern the naming and MCP ownership choices that the product-direction decision must settle.
